evidence.quote: Calder & Webb Builders
evidence.rationale: The preamble names Calder & Webb Builders as "Contractor".

evidence.quote: Brightline Glazing Co.
evidence.rationale: The preamble names Brightline Glazing Co. as "Subcontractor".

evidence.quote: Fresno Community Health Partners
evidence.rationale: The recital identifies the Prime Contract counterparty as "Owner".

evidence.quote: Kings Canyon Medical Office Building
evidence.rationale: The recital names the Project.

evidence.quote: This Subcontract is governed by the laws of the State of California.
evidence.rationale: Section 17.1 is the governing-law clause.

evidence.quote: The parties intend this Article to set the time for payment and not to make Owner's payment a condition precedent to Contractor's obligation to pay Subcontractor for Subcontract Work properly performed.
evidence.rationale: Section 6.3 sets payment at 10 days after Owner payment. Section 6.4 expressly says Owner payment is not a condition precedent.

evidence.quote: Contractor shall pay Subcontractor each progress payment within ten (10) days after Contractor receives payment from Owner for the Subcontract Work covered by that payment.
evidence.rationale: Section 6.3 states ten (10) days after receipt of Owner payment.

evidence.quote: The parties agree in writing that this ten (10) day period applies to progress payments under this Subcontract in place of the period otherwise provided by California Business and Professions Code Section 7108.5.
evidence.rationale: Section 6.3 states a specific period in writing.

evidence.quote: Contractor shall retain ten percent (10%) from each progress payment to Subcontractor.
evidence.rationale: Section 7.1 sets 10% retention, which is 1000 basis points.

release_condition.value: (a) Final Completion of the Subcontract Work, and (b) Contractor's receipt of retention from Owner attributable to the Subcontract Work

evidence.quote: Contractor shall release the retention to Subcontractor within ten (10) days after both of the following have occurred: (a) Final Completion of the Subcontract Work, and (b) Contractor's receipt of retention from Owner attributable to the Subcontract Work.
evidence.rationale: Section 7.2 sets the two triggers. Section 7.3 adds delivery of final releases and closeout documents, so the clauses must be read together.

evidence.quote: Contractor shall release the retention to Subcontractor within ten (10) days after both of the following have occurred
evidence.rationale: Section 7.2 states ten (10) days.

evidence.quote: Before Contractor makes any progress payment, Subcontractor shall deliver to Contractor a conditional waiver and release on progress payment covering the amount of that payment.
evidence.rationale: Section 8.1.

evidence.quote: Within five (5) days after receiving each progress payment, Subcontractor shall deliver to Contractor an unconditional waiver and release on progress payment covering the amount received.
evidence.rationale: Section 8.2.

evidence.quote: Subcontractor shall obtain from each of its Lower-Tier Parties, and deliver to Contractor, conditional and unconditional waivers and releases corresponding to the amounts paid to those Lower-Tier Parties.
evidence.rationale: Section 8.3.

evidence.quote: All waivers and releases delivered under this Subcontract, whether by Subcontractor or by its Lower-Tier Parties, shall be in the statutory forms set out in California Civil Code Sections 8132, 8134, 8136 and 8138, as applicable.
evidence.rationale: Section 8.4.

evidence.quote: Contractor may set off against any amount due to Subcontractor under this Subcontract all backcharges for costs Contractor incurs because of Subcontractor's failure to perform its obligations
evidence.rationale: Section 9.3 allows setoff of backcharges. Section 9.4 requires notice before a backcharge is incurred.

evidence.quote: Contractor may withhold from any payment an amount reasonably sufficient to cover the cost of correcting defective or nonconforming Subcontract Work that Subcontractor has not corrected.
evidence.rationale: Section 9.1. Section 9.2 also allows withholding for claims.

evidence.quote: Contractor will not pay for materials or equipment stored on site or off site that have not been incorporated into the Work.
evidence.rationale: Section 6.6 expressly excludes payment for stored materials.

anomalies.description: Retention release depends on Contractor's receipt of retention from Owner. The Section 6.4 disclaimer of an Owner-payment condition precedent refers only to "this Article" (Article 6, progress payments), not to Article 7 retention.

evidence.quote: (b) Contractor's receipt of retention from Owner attributable to the Subcontract Work.
evidence.rationale: Retention release depends on Contractor's receipt of retention from Owner. The Section 6.4 disclaimer of an Owner-payment condition precedent refers only to "this Article" (Article 6, progress payments), not to Article 7 retention.

anomalies.description: Release of retention carries additional conditions beyond Section 7.2: final lien and payment releases, and closeout documents.

evidence.quote: Release of retention is subject to Subcontractor's delivery of the final lien and payment releases required by Article 8 and the closeout documents required by Article 10.
evidence.rationale: Release of retention carries additional conditions beyond Section 7.2: final lien and payment releases, and closeout documents.

anomalies.description: Final Completion, a retention trigger, requires acceptance by Contractor and the Architect, which is a discretionary element.

evidence.quote: has been completed and accepted by Contractor and the Architect.
evidence.rationale: Final Completion, a retention trigger, requires acceptance by Contractor and the Architect, which is a discretionary element.

anomalies.description: Section 6.4 disclaims a condition precedent, but the payment clock runs only from Owner payment. No outside date is stated if Owner does not pay.

evidence.quote: Contractor shall pay Subcontractor each progress payment within ten (10) days after Contractor receives payment from Owner for the Subcontract Work covered by that payment.
evidence.rationale: Section 6.4 disclaims a condition precedent, but the payment clock runs only from Owner payment. No outside date is stated if Owner does not pay.

anomalies.description: Withholding rights are broad: they extend to reasonably anticipated claims and failure to maintain progress. Release of withheld amounts depends on Contractor's reasonable satisfaction.

evidence.quote: When the basis for a withholding has been eliminated to Contractor's reasonable satisfaction, Contractor shall pay the amount withheld with the next payment due to Subcontractor.
evidence.rationale: Withholding rights are broad: they extend to reasonably anticipated claims and failure to maintain progress. Release of withheld amounts depends on Contractor's reasonable satisfaction.

anomalies.description: If Owner terminates the Prime Contract, Subcontractor's recovery is limited to what Contractor recovers from Owner. This shifts Owner non-payment risk to Subcontractor in that scenario.

evidence.quote: Subcontractor's recovery shall be limited to the amount Contractor recovers from Owner on Subcontractor's behalf.
evidence.rationale: If Owner terminates the Prime Contract, Subcontractor's recovery is limited to what Contractor recovers from Owner. This shifts Owner non-payment risk to Subcontractor in that scenario.

anomalies.description: Change-order adjustments depend on Owner granting Contractor an adjustment, unless the change was caused by Contractor.

evidence.quote: Subcontractor shall not be entitled to an adjustment for changes for which Owner does not grant Contractor an adjustment, except to the extent the change was caused by Contractor.
evidence.rationale: Change-order adjustments depend on Owner granting Contractor an adjustment, unless the change was caused by Contractor.
